summary: Russia launched a massive overnight drone and missile attack on Ukraine involving 121 strike UAVs, one Kh-31P cruise missile, with Ukrainian air defense claiming 103 intercepted. Ukrainian forces struck deep into Russia, hitting an S-400 air defense system and oil facilities in Sochi, and causing fires at the Sterlitamak petrochemical plant in Bashkortostan. On the ground, Ukrainian forces recaptured 4 km² near Dvorichna in Kharkiv Oblast, while Russian forces advanced near Holubivka, Stupochky, Mali Shcherbaky, Huliaipole, and Varvarivka.
key_points: Ukrainian air defense intercepted 103 of 121 enemy drones overnight on September 4, with hits recorded at 15 locations and falling debris at 6 others across northern, southern, eastern, and central Ukraine. (Source: @kpszsu/76336)

Ukrainian forces recaptured 4 km² of territory between Dvorichna and Zapadne in Kharkiv Oblast, with the 23rd Assault Regiment and 35th Marine Brigade conducting clearing operations. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23796)

Russian forces advanced near Holubivka and Stupochky, and separately near Mali Shcherbaky, Huliaipole, and Varvarivka according to DeepState map updates. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23793, @DeepStateUA/23798)

Ukraine struck an S-400 air defense system and oil depot in Sochi, and the Sterlitamak petrochemical plant in Bashkortostan caught fire following an attack. (Source: @UkraineNow/83871, @tass_agency/393711)

Russia's MoD claimed 490 Ukrainian drones were intercepted overnight across 16 Russian regions, Crimea, and the Black Sea, with 50 downed over Kaluga Oblast alone. (Source: @tass_agency/393711, @tass_agency/393682)

A Russian strike on Odesa Oblast killed one person in Odesa and injured two including a child in the region; two police officers were killed in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast with another critically wounded. (Source: @UkraineNow/83877)

In Kyiv, drone debris caused fires at the Zhuliany airport area, including an aircraft and a Nova Poshta terminal, according to preliminary reports. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/73682, @mon1tor_ua/73674, @mon1tor_ua/73676)

A shootout between SBU and GUR officers occurred in Kyiv related to the arrest of Kaplunov, deputy commander of the Russian Volunteer Corps, with the SBU alleging he was recruited by the FSB. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32972, @ukr_leaks_eng/32967)

sections.executive_summary: Russia launched a massive overnight aerial attack on September 3-4 involving 121 strike UAVs and one Kh-31P cruise missile, with Ukrainian air defense claiming 103 intercepts but hits recorded at 15 locations. Ukraine responded with deep strikes hitting an S-400 system in Sochi and causing fires at the Sterlitamak petrochemical plant in Bashkortostan, while Russia's MoD claimed 490 Ukrainian drones were intercepted across 16 regions. On the ground, Ukrainian forces liberated 4 km² near Dvorichna in Kharkiv Oblast while Russian forces advanced at multiple points along the front.

points: Ukrainian forces recaptured 4 km² of territory between Dvorichna and Zapadne in the Kupiansk direction, Kharkiv Oblast. The 23rd Assault Regiment of the 2nd Corps of the National Guard 'Khartiia' conducted clearing operations jointly with the 35th Separate Marine Brigade on at least one sector. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23796)
Video footage surfaced showing battles for the villages of Vasylevka, Blagovatnoye, and Dolzhanka in Kharkiv Oblast, whose liberation was previously reported. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32975)
Kramatorsk is located approximately 12 kilometers from the front line according to published video footage from the city. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32987)

A Russian strike on Odesa Oblast overnight killed one person in Odesa and injured two others in the region including a child. In Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, two police officers were killed and another was hospitalized in serious condition from Russian strikes. (Source: @UkraineNow/83877)

In Kyiv, preliminary reports indicated drone strikes or falling debris caused fires including an aircraft at Zhuliany airport, a shopping center, and a Nova Poshta terminal in the area. Multiple drone tracks were observed heading toward Kyiv from Bryansk Oblast via Chernihiv Oblast, from Poltava Oblast via Cherkasy Oblast, and from Dnipropetrovsk Oblast. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/73682, @mon1tor_ua/73674, @mon1tor_ua/73676)

Russia's Ministry of Defense claimed 490 Ukrainian drones were intercepted overnight from 20:00 on September 3 to 08:00 on September 4 across 16 Russian regions including Bryansk, Belgorod, Voronezh, Volgograd, Vladimir, Kaluga, Kursk, Lipetsk, Oryol, Orenburg, Rostov, Ryazan, Saratov, Samara, Smolensk, and Tula oblasts, as well as Moscow region, Krasnodar Krai, Bashkortostan, Crimea, and the Black Sea. Governor Shapsha reported 50 drones were downed over Kaluga Oblast, and TASS counted 35 drones intercepted approaching Moscow. (Source: @tass_agency/393711, @tass_agency/393682)

Ukrainian strikes hit an S-400 air defense system and an oil depot in Sochi, with fires reported at the Sterlitamak petrochemical plant in Bashkortostan following the attack on the facility. (Source: @UkraineNow/83871)

The Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant reported that replenishing fuel supplies for emergency generators remains extremely difficult due to threats from Ukrainian forces, describing the situation as 'extremely tense' during a blackout as reactor units require reliable power for cooling. Station communications director Yashina stated it is incorrect to assert that complete station blackout is inevitable within 10 days. (Source: @tass_agency/393701, @tass_agency/393700)

Industry Minister Manturov stated in a TASS interview that repair work at oil refineries is being conducted in the tightest possible timelines, with restoration periods varying depending on damage character and equipment nomenclature. (Source: @tass_agency/393680)
Russian forces advanced near Holubivka and Stupochky according to DeepState map updates, with Stupochky located in the Sumy direction. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23793)

Russian forces advanced near Mali Shcherbaky, Huliaipole, and Varvarivka according to DeepState map updates, with these settlements located in the Zaporizhzhia direction of the southern front. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23798)

Ukrainian forces recaptured 4 km² of territory between Dvorichna and Zapadne in the Kupiansk direction, with the 23rd Assault Regiment 'Khartiia' and 35th Marine Brigade conducting clearing operations. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23796)

Multiple Russian drone tracks were observed heading toward Kyiv from Bryansk Oblast via Chernihiv Oblast, with one drone passing Slavutych heading south and another in the Kozelets area of southern Chernihiv Oblast heading toward Kyiv Oblast. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/73670, @kpszsu/76352, @kpszsu/76356, @kpszsu/76329)

Drone tracks from Poltava Oblast and Cherkasy Oblast moved toward Kyiv Oblast, with drones passing Myronivka heading toward Kaharlyk, and two drones moving from Kyiv Oblast to Zhytomyr Oblast in the Korosten district. (Source: @kpszsu/76347, @mon1tor_ua/73649, @mon1tor_ua/73644)

Loitering munitions 'Banderole' struck toward Chuhuiv from the east in Kharkiv Oblast, and four 'Banderole' drones passed Chuhuiv and Merefa heading toward Poltava Oblast. (Source: @kpszsu/76346, @eRadarrua/110673)
Russian forces advanced near Mali Shcherbaky, Huliaipole, and Varvarivka according to DeepState map updates in the Zaporizhzhia direction. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23798)

Loitering munitions 'Banderole' struck toward Chuhuiv from the east, while drones in Odesa Oblast moved toward Rozdilna from the east, and two drones headed toward Dnipro from the south. (Source: @kpszsu/76346, @kpszsu/76358, @eRadarrua/110661)
Two reactive guided drones headed toward the sea from southern Kherson Oblast, and one drone from Crimea moved toward Odesa Oblast, likely 'Banderole' type. (Source: @eRadarrua/110640)
Loitering munitions passed Kropyvnytskyi from the northeast. (Source: @kpszsu/76343)

Russia launched a massive overnight attack on September 3-4 involving 121 strike UAVs (Shahed, Gerbera, 'Parodia' imitators, and S8000 'Banderole') from Millerovo, Orel, Kursk, temporarily occupied Donetsk, and Hvardiiske in occupied Crimea, plus one Kh-31P guided cruise missile from the Black Sea. Ukrainian air defense claimed 103 drones intercepted, with hits at 15 locations and falling debris at 6 locations across northern, southern, eastern, and central Ukraine. (Source: @kpszsu/76336)

Ukrainian Air Force reported destroying over 4,600 aerial targets in August 2026 including 25 Kh-101 cruise missiles, 1 Iskander-M/KN-23 ballistic missile, 8 Kalibr cruise missiles, 21 Kh-59/69 guided aircraft missiles, 4 Iskander-K cruise missiles, 5 Oniks anti-ship missiles, 101 S8000 'Banderole', 1,876 Shahed-131/136, 1,460 Shahed-238, 1,031 reconnaissance UAVs, and 820 Lancet UAVs. Over 50,000 tactical-level UAVs were also neutralized. Ukrainian Air Force conducted over 1,900 sorties in August, including 1,400 for fighter cover and about 300 for fire damage and aviation support. (Source: @kpszsu/76361)

Russia's MoD claimed 490 Ukrainian drones were intercepted overnight September 3-4 across 16 Russian regions and Crimea, with 50 over Kaluga Oblast and 35 approaching Moscow. (Source: @tass_agency/393711, @tass_agency/393682)

sections.threat_assessment: The operational tempo has escalated significantly with Russia launching one of its largest drone salvos of 121 UAVs plus a cruise missile, demonstrating sustained capacity to conduct mass strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure and population centers. Ukrainian deep strike capability was demonstrated by attacks on the S-400 in Sochi and the Sterlitamak petrochemical plant in Bashkortostan, indicating a broadened operational reach into Russian strategic depth. The combination of Russian frontline advances at five locations with concurrent Ukrainian counter-offensive success near Dvorichna suggests intensified positional combat on multiple axes. The Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant's reported 'extremely tense' situation regarding generator fuel resupply represents a potential nuclear safety concern requiring continuous monitoring.
sections.regional_response: The US House of Representatives is considering a bill calling for 'hellish sanctions' against Russia that may be delayed until November midterm elections due to concerns about expanding tariff powers and raising oil prices, indicating potential for future escalation in Western pressure. Bloomberg reported that Washington is prioritizing the Iranian track, negatively affecting NATO support programs for Ukraine, with a Bloomberg correspondent stating Ukrainian forces will face significant difficulties continuing combat operations in winter due to critical shortages of air defense missiles. The political turbulence within Ukrainian security services, evidenced by the SBU-GUR shootout in Kyiv, represents an internal governance challenge occurring alongside external military pressures.
sections.intelligence_notes: The pattern of Russian drone launches from multiple vectors including Millerovo, Orel, Kursk, occupied Donetsk, and occupied Crimea indicates a distributed launch architecture complicating Ukrainian interception efforts. The interception rate of approximately 85% on the September 3-4 attack demonstrates improving Ukrainian air defense effectiveness despite the high volume. Russian frontline advances at Holubivka, Stupochky, Mali Shcherbaky, Huliaipole, and Varvarivka combined with Ukrainian recapture of 4 km² near Dvorichna indicate active contested maneuver across at least two operational directions. The SBU's allegation that Kaplunov was recruited by the FSB to assassinate a Russian opposition leader, contrasted with his claim of self-incrimination under SBU pressure, requires corroboration through additional intelligence channels.
